deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen, 1832–33. This is a laboratory log of the magnetic strength ('Kraftmaass') of steel bars, from the period of Gauss's absolute measurement of terrestrial magnetism (Intensitas vis magneticae, 1832) and the Gauss–Weber magnetometer work. It continues the table on fol. 177. The next page, dated 1833 April 30, concerns a galvanic chain.

(A) Table, columns 1–8 = bars 1–8. Each entry is a measured magnetic 'force measure', presumably proportional to the bar's magnetic moment as obtained by deflection or oscillation.
- Oct 19 (1832): bars 5–8 read 2720.9, 2690.7, 3000.3 (overwritten), 2883.9. A second line reads 2753.1, 2745.7, 3052.7, 2901.2.
- Oct 21: bars 5 and 6 read 2758.5, 2728.7, then 2722.1, 2718.0.
- Aug 16 (evidently 1833, entered later): bar 1 reads 2102.5 and 2269.1; bar 3 reads 2103.0; bars 5 and 6 read 2764.4, 2711.1.
- Sept 24: bar 1 reads 2478.9. A value 2171.6 stands under col. 4. Bars 5–8 read 2842.7, 2839.2, 3362.2, 336… (incomplete).
No computation is involved; these are raw data showing changes after re-stroking ('Bestreichung'), separation and so on.

(B) Kraftmaass of the small bars 'von Wertisch'.
- No. 2: 2138.2.
- No. 4: 2404.6.
- No. 3: 1284.0 (had been in one of the stroking bundles), then 2142.2 after new stroking.
- No. 2: 2173.6 after repeated stroking.
- No. 4: 2211.2 after being in the stroking bundle, then 2422.2 after repeated stroking.

(C) Weights in grams.
- Small bars: No. 2 = 336.8, No. 4 = 328.3, No. 3 = 345.1.
- Strong Leipzig bars: No. 21 = 1402; unmarked = 1312.5.
- Dimensions of No. 21 (mm): 363.0 × 38.3 × 12.6.
- The other Leipzig bar: length 363, width 38 or 35, thickness 13.0 or 11.0 (it is irregular or tapered).
- Large Wertisch bars: I = 1379.0, II = 1404.8.

(D) Reduction to a common weight of 400 g. Gauss computes the specific strength K_red = K × 400/m, using the latest K for each bar:
- No. 2: 2173.6 × 400/336.8 = 2581.47 ≈ 2581.5.
- No. 3: 2142.2 × 400/345.1 = 2482.99 ≈ 2483.0.
- No. 4: 2422.2 × 400/328.3 = 2951.20 ≈ 2951.2.
This is simple proportional scaling: moment per unit mass, so bars of different size can be compared as to quality of magnetisation.

Implicit check (mine): the volume of Leipzig bar 21 is 363 × 38.3 × 12.6 ≈ 175,177 mm³. With steel density about 7.8 g/cm³ this gives ≈ 1366 g, consistent with the weighed 1402 g. This confirms that the units are mm and g.
errors: No arithmetic errors: all three reductions to 400 g are correct to the stated decimal.
Chronology of the table is non-monotonic: Aug 16 and Sept 24 follow Oct 19/21. These are probably 1833 entries added later to the 1832 table, not a slip in computation.

results.what: Reduction of measured magnetic strengths of bars to a standard mass of 400 g (specific magnetism, moment per unit mass) to compare bar quality
results.modern_name: Specific magnetic moment / magnetization per unit mass
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber (Göttingen magnetic work, 1830s); the concept of comparing moment per unit mass is routine

results.what: Record of effects of re-stroking (Bestreichung) and storage in stroking bundles on bar magnetism
results.modern_name: Experimental magnetization of steel bars (touch method)
results.usually_credited_to: 18th-century practice (Knight, Michell, Coulomb); systematically logged by Gauss/Weber

deep.surprise_reason: Raw laboratory data and trivial proportional reduction from Gauss's well-documented magnetic experiments of 1832–33; nothing mathematically new.

checkable.asserts: Bar No. 2 reduced to 400 g gives 2581.5
Bar No. 3 reduced to 400 g gives 2483.0
Bar No. 4 reduced to 400 g gives about 2951.2 (last digit illegible on page)
Dimensions of Leipzig bar 21 (mm) with steel density about 7.8 g/cm^3 are consistent with its weighed 1402 g

transcription_corrections: Oct 19, col. 7: '3000' has been overwritten to read 3000.3. It is not a deletion followed by a new value.
Oct 21, col. 6: the third digit-group is overwritten (8 over 3); 2728.7 is the likely reading.
Sept 24 row: the value 2171.6 stands under column 4, not column 5. The last entry under col. 8 is the incomplete '336…'.
Reduced value for No. 4: the decimal digit is illegible; arithmetic gives 2951.2.
'gr' denotes grams. Dimensions are in millimetres, as confirmed by the mass/volume check.
